faqs.question: What is CAP2000+ used for?

faqs.question: What's the difference between the L Series and H Series?

sections.tabSummary: How L and H Series fit different testing needs
body: How CAP2000+'s variable speed range and dual temperature series fit different testing needs.
High-shear viscosity testing rarely happens at a single fixed speed or temperature, and CAP2000+ is built to cover a genuinely wide operating window rather than a narrow one.

Variable speed runs from 5 to 1000 RPM, wide enough to move between exploratory R&D testing and repeatable QC protocols on the same instrument. Temperature control runs through a built-in Peltier plate, split across two model series depending on what a formulation actually needs: the L Series covers 5°C to 75°C for standard ambient-to-moderate testing, while the H Series reaches all the way to 235°C for genuinely high-temperature materials like hot melt adhesives or asphalt. Both series pair that temperature control with the same wide shear rate range, keeping the instrument well suited to small sample volumes where precise, repeatable conditions matter.

faqs.question: What is the DVNext Cone/Plate Rheometer used for?
faqs.answer: It's a rheometer for precise absolute viscosity measurement of small sample volumes, used in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, cosmetics, and specialty chemical R&D where sample material is limited or expensive.

faqs.question: How small a sample does it need?
faqs.answer: As small as 0.5–2.0 mL.

faqs.question: How does it calculate viscosity?
faqs.answer: It measures the torque required to rotate a cone spindle immersed in the sample against a plate; that torque is proportional to shear stress and is used to calculate absolute viscosity in centipoise (mPa·s).

faqs.question: What is the torque measurement accuracy and repeatability?
faqs.answer: 1% of full-scale range for accuracy, and 0.2% of full-scale range for repeatability.

faqs.question: How is the spindle attached?
faqs.answer: Via a magnetic coupling attachment, simplifying attachment and removal and minimizing handling errors.

faqs.question: Does the instrument require manual gap adjustment?
faqs.answer: No. Electronic gap adjustment reduces manual intervention and improves repeatability.

faqs.question: What do the auto-zero and auto-range functions do?
faqs.answer: Auto-zero automatically calibrates the instrument for optimal torque accuracy; auto-range automatically defines the full-scale range for every spindle/speed combination.

faqs.question: Why is temperature control faster on this instrument?
faqs.answer: The small sample volume has less thermal mass, so it reaches target temperature faster than larger-volume viscometry, reducing wait time during testing.

faqs.question: Is external gauging needed to set the cone/plate gap?
faqs.answer: No. The relative cone-to-plate position is maintained through simple mechanical setup without external gauges.

faqs.question: Can multiple cone spindles be used?
faqs.answer: Yes, multiple cone spindles are supported and can be calibrated for specific applications.

faqs.question: Is 21 CFR Part 11 compliance available?
faqs.answer: Yes, as an optional feature, including electronic signatures, audit trails, and secure data management.

faqs.question: Can the instrument connect to a LIMS?
faqs.answer: Yes, optional Ethernet and LIMS connectivity is available for integration with laboratory management systems.

faqs.question: How is DVNext Cone/Plate different from DV2Plus?
faqs.answer: DVNext Cone/Plate is built specifically for small sample volumes (0.5–2.0 mL) using cone/plate geometry. DV2Plus is a general-purpose rotational spindle viscometer with a 740-speed range and built-in Gel Timer functionality, suited to larger, more readily available sample volumes.

Standard rotational viscometry generally assumes sample volume isn't the constraint — there's enough material to fill a beaker and immerse a spindle. Cone/plate geometry doesn't need that assumption. DVNext Cone/Plate measures accurate absolute viscosity from 0.5 to 2.0 mL, which is the difference between testing being possible and testing consuming more of a limited or expensive material than a project can afford.

That small volume carries a second benefit beyond conservation: thermal mass is proportionally small too, so temperature adjustments happen quickly. A test sequence that steps through multiple temperature points doesn't spend most of its time waiting for the sample to equilibrate — it spends that time collecting data instead, directly improving throughput for iterative formulation work.

Small volume also means fast thermal equilibrium: temperature adjustments happen quickly, cutting the wait time that larger sample volumes impose between test conditions.

A magnetic coupling attachment turns spindle changes into a simple placement rather than a fiddly mechanical fitting, and electronic gap adjustment removes manual setup from the equation entirely — both reducing handling error and speeding throughput. Torque measurement holds to 1% of full-scale range accuracy with 0.2% repeatability, on the same 7-inch touchscreen interface found across the DVNext line, with optional 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and LIMS connectivity for regulated environments.

Buying more compliance capability than a lab actually needs adds cost and complexity without adding value; buying too little means a regulated workflow has to be retrofitted later. DVNext Rheometer avoids that mismatch by offering the choice upfront rather than layering compliance on as an afterthought.

The Standard version is built for straightforward, high-quality measurement: digital leveling and a Start-up Wizard get a test running quickly, Gel-Timer functionality is built in rather than an add-on, and magnetic coupling or a barcode scanner can be added where the workflow calls for them. The Compliant version starts from a different assumption — that every test needs to be traceable, auditable, and connected to a system of record — and builds magnetic coupling, hand-held barcode scanning with automatic accessory detection, Ethernet and LIMS connectivity, and non-editable PDF reporting into the standard configuration rather than treating any of them as optional extras.

body: The accuracy and repeatability figures matched against DV2Plus.

Entry-level instrumentation usually signals a trade-off somewhere in the measurement chain — a wider accuracy band, fewer discrete speeds, a narrower operating range. DVPlus doesn't carry that trade-off into its core specification: ±1.0% of range accuracy and ±0.2% repeatability, identical to what Brookfield states for the DV2Plus, and a full 740-speed range rather than a reduced subset.

What positions DVPlus as the entry-level instrument is everything built around that core measurement, not the measurement itself. A 5-inch display instead of 7 inches, no stated Viscosity Wizard or built-in Gel Timer functionality, and a simpler connectivity story via the DVPlus Connect App rather than DV360's advanced compliance-ready software layer. For a lab whose real requirement is accurate, repeatable viscosity data without needing guided complex-test setup or regulated audit trails, that's the right trade to make.

paragraphs: Some testing protocols care less about a single-point viscosity reading and more about how a material's behaviour changes over time — how long it takes to reach a target torque, how long temperature equilibration actually takes, or when a test sequence should stop based on a defined condition rather than a fixed duration. DVPlus provides direct access to those three time-based functions rather than requiring them to be configured through a more general step-program interface.

Automatic range calculation works alongside that: the Full-Scale Range at 100% and the maximum measurable viscosity for a given spindle/speed combination are calculated automatically, removing a manual lookup step from method setup and reducing the chance of a test running outside its valid measurement range without the operator noticing.

Running that measurement as a bolt-on to a general viscometer, or on a separate dedicated instrument, adds a step and a potential source of inconsistency between the viscosity data and the gel time data.

DVNext Rheometer with Gel Timer Functionality keeps both on the same measurement platform. Gel-Timer functionality is positioned as a defining capability rather than an incidental feature, so gelation studies and standard viscosity/yield stress testing draw on the same calibration, the same interface, and the same reporting path.

heroParagraphs: Dial Reading Viscometer is Brookfield's original viscosity measurement instrument, in continuous production since 1934. Current models use a multi-speed electronic drive with an ergonomic speed control knob, giving quick selection across 10 pre-set speeds on standard models (8 speeds on LVT models). The direct drive design runs quietly and works across global power sources.

Torque measurement accuracy is 1% of the full-scale range, with repeatability of 0.2% of the full-scale range. Continuous torque sensing gives real-time readings throughout a test. Speed adjustment and on/off control are direct, with no menu navigation involved. The instrument is fully compatible with the Brookfield accessory range, and NIST traceable viscosity standards are available.
